correctness.rationale: Conditioning the uniform simplex on all coordinates exceeding t gives exactly the affine image t1+(1-mt)X, with volume factor (1-mt)^(m-1). Along this affine path the power sum is strictly Schur-convex for a>1 and strictly Schur-concave for 0<a<1, giving the sign theorem through the survival-integral covariance identity. For integer q, Beta moments and a finite binomial expansion yield the displayed mixed moment and covariance. Exact direct simplex integrals for m=2 and m=3, plus broad rational recurrence/formula checks, agree with the derivation.

value.rationale: Minimum spacing is a canonical extreme-spacing statistic, while power-spacing sums include the classical Greenwood goodness-of-fit statistic and a broad family of dispersion measures. The theorem identifies a sharp structural sign transition at power one, supplies exact finite mixed moments for every integer power, and gives an interpretable threshold regression showing how excluding tiny gaps forces Greenwood dispersion toward equal spacing. This connects local clustering and global spacing dispersion rather than adding a single isolated covariance.
